absent: Numeric values and bit positions of cache, lookup, mount and inode flags and of reported error outcomes.
Implementation of parent comparison, entry revalidation, transit management, automount and filesystem lookup operations.
Definitions of hash bucket selection, hash mixing, table sizes and sequence counter mechanics.
Reference counting, mount propagation, group identity handling and namespace ownership transfer beyond observed effects.
Symlink following, link stack handling, root legitimization and unlink race detection internals.
Full lock ordering and deadlock avoidance across entry, inode, mount and namespace protection.
Complete layouts of traversal, entry, inode, mount and mountpoint objects beyond observed linkage.

findings.text: Hashed entry search keyed by parent identity and name hash. A successful result is a live entry with an extra reference held by the caller. Failure to match yields absence. Matching requires hashed state, identical parent, equal hash value and name equality. Concurrent table mutation is tolerated, with false absence possible under concurrent rename unless the caller applies outer rename sequencing.

Name equality service for a candidate entry against a wanted name in the context of a parent. When the parent advertises no custom comparison, equality means equal length and equal bytes. When custom comparison is advertised, the decision is delegated to the parent supplied operation. The outcome is boolean.

Parallel-safe allocation for name resolution that guarantees convergence on a single pending entry per parent and name. Races against completed entries return the completed entry and discard the fresh allocation. Races against pending entries block until the peer completes and then either accept the completed hashed match or restart. Fresh entries appear as children of the parent and inherit disconnected marking, with allocation failure reported as out of memory.

Installation service for automount results. A null input means success with no action, while an error input is propagated. A result whose root equals the trigger point is rejected as a loop. Contention that leaves the exact mount lock busy is treated as benign success. Otherwise the supplied tree is installed with shrinkable marking.

When custom name comparison is active, lock-free hash scanning samples candidate length and bytes as a consistent pair under entry sequencing and retries the sample when concurrent modification is detected. Only a stable sample is presented to the parent comparison operation. Success returns the entry together with its sequence for later revalidation.

Hash chain walks are protected by read-side critical sections. Candidates that require stability against moves are examined with the candidate lock held, and references are acquired while that lock is held. Purely lock-free sampling instead relies on sequence begin and retry without acquiring the candidate lock.
Slow resolution executes with the directory held in shared mode for the entire slow operation, released afterward. Resolution is refused when the directory is observed dead.

Pending resolution state moves from flagged fresh, to published in the pending table, to waited upon by peers, to completed with wakeup. Completion clears pending state, removes the entry from the pending table and wakes waiters. Waiters recheck hash, parent, hashed state and name after wakeup and restart on any mismatch.

Slow allocation distinguishes completed versus pending outcomes. Completed entries undergo revalidation where a zero outcome invalidates and restarts, a negative outcome is returned, and a positive outcome continues. Pending entries trigger filesystem lookup followed by completion marking, with any returned alias substituted for the allocated entry and reference ownership transferred.

Conversion from lock-free to referenced traversal succeeds only when mount sequencing remains valid, parent and child references are acquired while live, child sequencing is unchanged and the root remains legitimate, after which lock-free mode is left. Any miss leaves lock-free mode, clears path state as appropriate and reports failure so the caller retries in referenced mode, with sequence mismatch additionally releasing the child reference.

Mount-aware stepping treats unmanaged positive entries as continuable without further work and unmanaged negative entries as missing. Managed entries may invoke filesystem transit handling, switch to a covering mount with reference exchange, or trigger automount creation. A request that forbids crossing is honored, a directory indication from automount handling is normalized to success, and the jumped indication tracks whether mount switching occurred.

Automount triggering is suppressed for plain attribute queries of positive entries unless directory, parent, open, create or explicit automount intent is present, and is always suppressed when crossing is disabled. Excessive link following depth fails as a loop. Otherwise the filesystem automount operation supplies a tree that proceeds to installation.

Exact mountpoint locking uses a pinned object that releases automatically on scope exit. Mountpoint table lookup and insertion are serialized by mount sequencing in exclusive mode. Recursive attachment additionally serializes hash publication with a dedicated hash lock and orders propagation and sharing changes before publication, with cleanup that unmounts propagated copies and clears pending counts on failure.

Concurrent renames can cause hash walks to miss entries and report false absence, which outer rename sequencing must detect. Odd directory sequencing indicates ongoing modification and forces retry. Pending-table insertion rechecks directory sequencing while holding the bucket lock to close the race between lookup and publication.

Lookup and mount handling distinguish missing, stale, crossing-disabled, busy, invalid, not-directory, loop and retry-request outcomes. Stale covers unlink races revealed during referenced stepping, crossing-disabled covers mount or automount attempts under a no-crossing request, busy covers duplicate filesystem placement, and retry-request covers lock-free validation misses that require referenced retry.

Observed relationships link entries to a parent, to sibling and children membership, to hash and pending-hash membership, to name bytes with length and hash, to a sequence counter, to a lock with reference count, to flags and operations and to an inode. Traversal state pairs a mount with an entry plus sequencing and link depth. Mounts associate a superblock, a root, a mountpoint, a parent, a namespace and flags, with overmount chaining for stacked mounts.
Dead directory state is defined by presence of dead marking S_DEAD in the inode flag word.

Slow name resolution and mount-aware stepping serve as internal traversal entries. Slow resolution expects a directory and wanted name with shared directory protection. Stepping accepts traversal state plus a candidate entry, with a fast path for lock-free traversal over unmanaged non-symlink entries and delegation to slow handling for mounts, symlinks and referenced mode.
Shared directory protection corresponds to read acquisition of the directory semaphore, with release corresponding to read release.

Attached state holds exactly when the mount namespace pointer is present, distinguishing attached mounts from detached versus internal ones. Anonymous namespace state holds when the dedicated flag is set. The effective covering mount is found by following overmount links to the end.

Mount installation strips internal flag bits, refuses superblocks marked against user mounts, requires equal directory-ness between mountpoint and new root, rejects identical superblock with identical mountpoint root as busy, and rejects symlink roots as invalid. Parents lacking validity are rejected except for shrinkable automounts whose mountpoint remains attached.

Pinned mountpoint acquisition reuses an existing table entry when the target already serves as a mountpoint and is still linked, failing as missing when unlinked. Otherwise it marks the target as a mountpoint, retrying lookup when another party wins the mark and failing when the target cannot serve, then publishes a new table entry with reference held and list state initialized.
